CVE-2026-124758.title: Integer underflow of the record data length in IODWrite requests
CVE-2026-124758.description: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.

Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. The absence of timeouts also permitted resource-exhaustion against the server's outbound connection pool.

CVE-2026-33203.title: SiYuan has an Unauthenticated WebSocket DoS via Auth Keepalive Bypass
CVE-2026-33203.description: SiYuan is a personal knowledge management system. Prior to version 3.6.2, the SiYuan kernel WebSocket server accepts unauthenticated connections when a specific "auth keepalive" query parameter is present. After connection, incoming messages are parsed using unchecked type assertions on attacker-controlled JSON. A remote attacker can send malformed messages that trigger a runtime panic, potentially crashing the kernel process and causing denial of service. Version 3.6.2 fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-95823.title: Use-after-free and net_buf leak in Zephyr TCP header linearization (tcp_pkt_linearize)
CVE-2026-95823.description:
tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf. While pulling the header bytes out of the following fragments, the loop called net_buf_unref() on an emptied fragment without first detaching its frags pointer. net_buf_unref() walks the whole fragment list, so the payload buffers still linked behind that fragment were freed as well, and the stale pointer was then reinstalled into the packet as buf->frags, producing a use-after-free and a later double free during packet teardown. The same loop also advanced to second->frags unconditionally: when the fragment still held payload after the header remainder was pulled, it was spliced out of the packet without ever being unreferenced, permanently leaking that buffer and silently dropping the data it carried.

CVE-2026-99531.title: ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header
CVE-2026-99531.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header

When an encrypted request comes in, the decryption key is picked by
the SessionId in the transform header, but the request is then
authorized under whatever session the decrypted inner header names.
Nothing ever compares the two, so on a connection with more than
one session a client can get a request decrypted with one session's
key and run it as another session. Encrypted requests are exempt
from signing too, so a valid AEAD tag is the only proof of session
identity, and it is checked against the wrong session.

MS-SMB2 says the server must check that the transform SessionId
matches the one in the decrypted SMB2 header and treat a mismatch
as a protocol error. Add that check in __handle_ksmbd_work() after
decryption, before dispatching: the message has to be at least one
fixed SMB2 header, the first operation must not set
SMB2_FLAGS_RELATED_OPERATIONS…

CVE-2026-99544.title: Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices
CVE-2026-99544.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices

In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and
write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as
potentially malicious.

hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds
checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset
up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too:
the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how
much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than
the ring.

The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated
snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices,
hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO.

CVE-2026-99629.title: drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih
CVE-2026-99629.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih

Port this change to navi10_ih.c:
commit afbf7955ff01 ("drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts")

Setting IH_RB_WPTR to 0 does not clear RB_OVERFLOW if RB_ENABLE is not
set. Pulse WPTR_OVERFLOW_CLEAR after RB_ENABLE (and with
WPTR_OVERFLOW_ENABLE) so overflow is cleared when interrupts are
enabled.

(cherry picked from commit 713fb4ab04f4d2af6120f8eb607c5673b2759b38)

CVE-2026-99760.title: batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes
CVE-2026-99760.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes

A received TT change (OGM diff or full table response) with the ROAM flag
but without DEL is handled by batadv_tt_global_add() like a ROAMING_ADV:

* a newly created global entry gets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM and is
therefore excluded from the global CRC. The sender has it in its local
CRC and the receiver has to request the full table again
* batadv_tt_global_purge_local() removes the local entry of the
receiver. The receiver's own client is considered as roamed to the sender
and frames for it are rerouted

The ROAM flag only has a meaning together with DEL. Drop it on reception to
keep it from populating the global table with a temporary ROAMING entry
which is not part of the CRC - and therefore causing a CRC mismatch.
